PHP-HLV-24-001, Understanding Drug Use in Waterloo Region
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner of Public Health & Paramedic Services/Medical Officer of Health, introduced the presentation on PHP-HLV-24-001, Understanding Drug Use in Waterloo Region. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. James Macintosh, Manager of Information, Planning & Foundational Standards, highlighted the importance of collaboration between all levels of government to address issues related to drug use. He provided a brief overview of current drug use data in the Region of Waterloo such as suspected opioid-related drug overdose deaths. Katie MacDonald, Manager of Health System Integration & Strategic Partnerships, further highlighted the contributing factors to high-risk drug use including housing instability or mental health illnesses. In 2023, the Chief Medical Officer of Health recommended that high-risk drug use be addressed by an all-of-society, health first approach through prevention, harm reduction, treatment and recovery, and justice and enforcement. Rhonda Nicholls, Director of Strategy, Performance & Organizational Standards, concluded the presentation by noting that several initiatives including the Canadian Drugs and Substances Strategy, Ontario Harm Reduction Distribution program, and various grants. She also noted next steps such as providing mandated harm reduction services and working toward an integrated community approach that involves all-levels of government.

In response to the Committee, J. Macintosh explained that the estimated statistic on 9,219 individuals using drugs in the Region of Waterloo. R. Nicholls further explained that upstream access to treatment is person driven.

Responding to the Committee, Dr. Wang explained that the success of reducing the harms from high-risk drug use is difficult to establish through statistical data and it would be unlikely to reduce harmful drug use to zero. J. Macintosh noted that needle syringe program can be used as a measure of addiction, but data related to drug use in housing shelters is not readily available. 

In response to the Committee, Dr. Wang confirmed that public health agencies across Ontario have found that the types and combination of drugs being used have become more toxic which result in an increase to overdose and she further confirmed that safe supply programs are currently being assessed by Health Canada to determine its applicability on a larger scale.

The Committee highlighted the importance of having measurable benchmarks to monitor high-risk drug use, such as wastewater surveillance. Dr. Wang noted that there are measurables that monitor the effectiveness of harm reduction and prevention to monitor such as the Ontario Naloxone Program, but more intervention is still required. Cameron Dearlove, Waterloo Region integrated Drug Strategy Chairperson, also highlighted that estimated drug use is approximately 10,000. Wastewater surveillance has assisted WRIDS on mitigating extremely toxic drug use and using it as an opportunity to provide information on drugs currently being used in the community. C. Dearlove further highlighted various supports throughout the Region and the need to enhance these programs. 

In response to the Committee, C. Dearlove confirmed that WRIDS was a co-creator in the creation of the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness. They further confirmed that housing shelters can receive a federal designation for a consumption and treatment services site based on urgent need. J. Macintosh and Dr. Wang explained that the Office of the Chief Coroner provides the data and reports for drug related deaths. 

Received for information.
